constructedResponseWorkshops.title: Scaffolding claim-evidence unity and overcoming writer’s block in 8th-grade persuasive writing
constructedResponseWorkshops.prompt: Supporting an 8th-grade persuasive-writing workshop under teacher direction, design brief coaching moves for one student whose draft lacks source attribution and paragraph unity and another student frozen by a blank screen.
constructedResponseWorkshops.stimulus: During an 8th-grade persuasive workshop on extending library hours, the teacher asks you to check in with 3 students using the class organizer and rubric. One student states a clear claim, then pastes two unattributed statistics from a class packet without explaining them and pivots mid-paragraph to cafeteria complaints. Another stares at a blank screen for 10 minutes saying, "I have ideas, I just cannot start."
taskParts: A. Diagnose the organizational, evidence-integration, and prewriting-initiation barriers shown by the two students.
B. Plan targeted, teacher-aligned scaffolds for paragraph unity, basic source attribution and reasoning, and low-friction drafting entry that preserve each student’s voice.
C. Clarify how you will coordinate authorized accessibility tools and report progress to the supervising teacher without stepping outside paraprofessional scope.

planningFrame.label: Evidence
planningFrame.guidance: Distinguish the drafting-organization issue (unattributed packet statistics, missing warrant/explanation, and off-topic cafeteria detour) from the prewriting initiation barrier (oral ideas present, blank-page freeze).

planningFrame.label: Instructional principle
planningFrame.guidance: Support the writing process—planning, drafting, and revising—with audience-aware claim-evidence-reasoning organizers and oral-to-written bridges while keeping every argument and sentence student-authored.

planningFrame.label: Support plan
planningFrame.guidance: Guide Student 1 to color-code sentences against the library-hours claim, cut/move the cafeteria lines, add simple source tags ("According to the class packet"), and write one "This shows why" link; invite Student 2 to talk through 3 bullet ideas on the teacher’s organizer or use permitted speech-to-text before drafting a rough opener.

planningFrame.label: Check & follow-up
planningFrame.guidance: Check back in 8 minutes to verify Student 1 added attribution/explanation and Student 2 moved from bullets to an opening claim, then share brief conference notes with the teacher rather than scoring the rubric.

successCriteria: Addresses all three issues in Student 1’s paragraph: identifying the off-topic cafeteria drift, adding clear attribution to the class packet, and explaining how the statistics prove the library-hours claim.

Unblocks Student 2 through oral brainstorming, teacher-provided graphic-organizer bullets, or pre-approved accessibility tools (such as speech-to-text if authorized) instead of dictating an introductory paragraph.
Uses the classroom teacher’s existing organizer and rubric criteria as anchor points without altering assignment expectations or scoring the essay.
Includes a concrete short-interval check-in and concise status report back to the supervising teacher.
commonPitfalls: Dictating an opening hook and thesis statement for the stalled student to type word-for-word.
Allowing unattributed statistics to stand on their own without prompting the student to credit the class packet and explain their relevance to the claim.
Focusing first on minor spelling or comma fixes while the paragraph still veers off topic into cafeteria complaints.
Telling the students what rubric score or letter grade their drafts would earn instead of leaving formal evaluation to the teacher.
sampleOutline: Conference diagnosis: Student 1 has a clear claim but drops in unattributed, unexplained statistics and breaks unity with cafeteria complaints; Student 2 has oral ideas but needs an initiation bridge.

Revision support (Student 1): check each sentence against the library-hours claim, relocate or cut the cafeteria detour, add a packet source tag ("According to the district survey in our packet"), and prompt a one-sentence "This matters because" explanation.

Prewriting support (Student 2): shift from the blank screen to the teacher’s organizer—have the student speak their position and two reasons aloud while jotting 3 short phrases (or using authorized speech-to-text) to draft a rough starting sentence.
Follow-up & scope: return after 8 minutes to affirm independent momentum, never assign rubric grades, and brief the teacher on source-citation and drafting-start needs.
constructedResponseWorkshops.reviewNote: Independent applied case-analysis practice; not an official ETS prompt, rubric, score, pass prediction, or licensure/employment determination. AlloFlow does not score written responses.

quickReference.title: Reading Comprehension & Teacher-Directed Literacy Support
quickReference.purpose: Anchors passage comprehension skills, text-feature navigation, and compliant paraprofessional reading-support boundaries.
checklist: Check whether the question tests direct passage comprehension (main idea, detail, vocabulary, text feature) or classroom reading-support application.
For classroom scenarios, verify the student's exact skill breakdown (phonemic awareness, phonics/decoding, fluency, vocabulary, or comprehension).
Confirm that the paraprofessional action reinforces teacher-assigned instruction rather than independently diagnosing, grading, or changing curriculum.
formulas: Reading skill progression: Phonological/Phonemic Awareness (spoken sounds, no print) → Phonics (sound-letter decoding) → Fluency (accuracy, rate, expression) → Vocabulary → Comprehension.
Context-clue & structural decoding anchors: use surrounding definitions, synonyms, antonyms, and examples alongside prefixes, roots, and suffixes to guide students to word meaning.

Text-feature navigation rules: Table of Contents locates broad chapters at the front; Index locates specific terms by page at the back; Glossary defines domain terms; Headings/Captions organize key ideas.
ParaPro literacy scope rule: paraprofessionals reinforce teacher-planned lessons, prompt decoding strategies, model fluent read-alouds, and record reading observations for the supervising teacher.
decisionRules: When a student misreads an unfamiliar multisyllabic word during guided oral reading → prompt the student to sound out word parts, syllabicate, or check context rather than immediately supplying the word or assigning new curriculum.

When a student reads accurately but slowly and robotically without pausing at punctuation → support fluency with teacher-approved repeated reading, echo reading, or choral reading at an appropriate level.
When a student struggles with identifying spoken beginning or rhyming sounds → use oral sound-blending or segmenting activities (phonemic awareness) rather than silent dictionary worksheets.
When a student shows persistent comprehension breakdown or requests an IEP accommodation change → log objective reading behaviors and share them with the classroom teacher immediately.
cautions: Never choose an option where the paraprofessional selects a brand-new reading program, diagnoses dyslexia, or holds a formal parent evaluation conference independently.
Do not confuse phonemic awareness (purely auditory manipulation of phonemes) with phonics (connecting phonemes to written graphemes).
Avoid selecting a passage detail as the main idea when it only backs up one paragraph.

quickReference.title: Foundational Math Computation & Classroom Math Support
quickReference.purpose: Anchors core arithmetic, fractions/percents, measurement, basic algebra/data formulas, and paraprofessional math-tutoring boundaries.
checklist: Determine whether the item requires direct numerical computation or diagnosing a student's procedural error during guided math practice.
Align place values, common denominators, and measurement units before computing or checking student work.
Verify that any classroom math intervention scaffolds student thinking with teacher-approved tools instead of doing steps for the student.
formulas: Fraction, decimal & percent equivalence: a/b ÷ c/d = (a/b) × (d/c); add/subtract fractions via LCD; decimal-to-percent shifts decimal two places right; benchmark equivalents 1/8 = 12.5%, 1/4 = 25%, 1/3 ≈ 33.3%, 3/4 = 75%.
Basic algebra & proportions: solve one- and two-step equations by inverse operations in reverse PEMDAS order; proportional scaling a/b = c/d gives a × d = b × c.
Everyday geometry & measurement: Rectangle P = 2(l + w), A = lw; Triangle A = (1/2)bh; Rectangular prism V = lwh; elapsed time counts forward by whole hours then remaining minutes (1 hr = 60 min).

ParaPro math-support rule: diagnose the exact procedural misconception (place-value misalignment, regrouping error, inverted ratio), model with teacher-provided manipulatives or number lines, and report recurring gaps to the teacher.
decisionRules: When a student adds 1/3 + 1/4 and writes 2/7 → recognize the missing common-denominator misconception and guide the student to represent equivalent twelfths with visual fraction strips.
When a student solves 3x + 4 = 19 by adding 4 instead of subtracting 4 → prompt the student to check with inverse operations and substitute the result back into the original equation.
When a word problem asks how much more or how many remain after spending → verify all multi-step quantities and units before performing subtraction.

When a student repeatedly cannot complete grade-level math tasks even with scaffolding → document the exact error pattern and confer with the supervising teacher rather than altering grading criteria.
cautions: Never round intermediate decimal values too early when multiple steps remain, as early rounding shifts the final answer choice.
Do not confuse perimeter (distance around a figure) with area (square units covering the interior).
Avoid completing calculations for the student or introducing an unapproved shortcut method that conflicts with the teacher's lesson objective.

quickReference.title: Grammar, Editing, Writing Process & Classroom Support
quickReference.purpose: Anchors standard English editing rules, writing-process stages, and paraprofessional boundaries when coaching student writers.
checklist: Read the full sentence or paragraph to distinguish surface mechanics errors (spelling, capitalization, punctuation) from organization and clarity issues.
Identify which writing-process stage the student is currently in (prewriting, drafting, revising, editing, or publishing) before selecting feedback.
Ensure paraprofessional coaching preserves student ownership of the writing and follows the teacher's rubric.
formulas: Writing process sequence: Prewriting (brainstorming/outlining) → Drafting (getting ideas down) → Revising (improving organization, focus, details, word choice) → Editing/Proofreading (correcting grammar, spelling, punctuation) → Publishing.

Core editing checks: complete sentences (subject + predicate, no fragments or run-ons), subject-verb agreement, consistent verb tense, correct apostrophe use (possessives vs. contractions), and homophones (their/there/they're, your/you're, its/it's).
Paragraph structure check: clear topic sentence + relevant supporting details in logical sequence + concluding sentence, with off-topic sentences removed during revision.

ParaPro writing scope rule: ask guiding questions, use teacher-provided checklists or graphic organizers, help students spot patterns of errors themselves, and never rewrite essays or assign final grades.
decisionRules: When a student is in the prewriting or early drafting stage and stalls over spelling → encourage completing ideas with a graphic organizer first and save mechanics proofreading for the editing stage.
When a student's draft contains repeated run-on sentences → model how to locate complete thoughts and separate them with periods or conjunctions, then have the student edit the remaining sentences.
When an exam item asks which revision improves paragraph unity → remove sentences that introduce unrelated trivia and add transitions connecting supporting details to the topic sentence.

When a student asks whether a draft deserves an A or meets IEP writing goals → refer final evaluation and rubric scoring to the supervising teacher while offering specific formative checklist feedback.
cautions: Do not confuse revising (big-picture content, clarity, organization, and word choice) with editing (surface conventions like commas, capitalization, and spelling).
Never add an apostrophe to make a regular noun plural (teachers, not teacher's) or to possessive pronouns (hers, ours, theirs, its).
Avoid taking the pencil to rewrite a student's paragraph yourself, which removes student learning and crosses paraprofessional instructional boundaries.

misconceptionFamilies.label: Confusing Passage Main Idea with Supporting Details or Outside Assumptions
misconceptionFamilies.description: Answering ParaPro reading comprehension items using real-world background beliefs that never appear in the passage, or choosing a single vivid fact from a table, notice, or paragraph instead of the overarching main idea or strictly text-supported inference.
misconceptionFamilies.remediationMove: Point directly to the sentence or table row that proves your answer: discard any option that sounds reasonable in everyday life but lacks explicit textual support, and separate fact from opinion using verifiable evidence.

misconceptionFamilies.label: Adding Fraction Denominators Directly and Misapplying Percent or Decimal Place Value
misconceptionFamilies.description: Adding or subtracting fractions straight across (treating 3/4 + 1/8 as 4/12), misaligning decimal place value when dividing by a decimal (4.8 ÷ 0.6) or comparing tenths/hundredths, or taking a percentage of the wrong whole without calculator support.
misconceptionFamilies.remediationMove: Convert unlike fractions to a common denominator before adding numerators only, scale both divisor and dividend by the same power of 10 to clear decimal divisors, and anchor percents to parts per 100 of the specified whole.

misconceptionFamilies.label: Breaking Equation Balance, Order of Operations, and Area vs. Perimeter Distinctions
misconceptionFamilies.description: Evaluating arithmetic expressions strictly left to right (computing 18 − 3 × 4 as 15 × 4 = 60), expanding exponents as multiplication by the exponent (2⁵ as 2 × 5 = 10), breaking equality by performing an operation on only one side of an equation, or confusing perimeter boundary length with enclosed area.
misconceptionFamilies.remediationMove: Follow order of operations (grouping → exponents → multiplication/division left to right → addition/subtraction left to right), apply every inverse operation to both sides of an equation, and distinguish perimeter (sum of outer sides in linear units) from area (interior square units).

misconceptionFamilies.label: Missing Comma Splices, Homophone Mix-Ups, and Subject-Verb Agreement Errors
misconceptionFamilies.description: Overlooking commonly confused words ("their/there/they're," "then/than," "its/it's"), misplacing plural possessive apostrophes ("two teachers' lesson plans"), pairing a verb with a nearby object instead of the subject, or joining two independent clauses with a bare comma.
misconceptionFamilies.remediationMove: Expand every contraction mentally ("they are," "it is") to test homophones, locate the true subject apart from modifying phrases, check whether possession is singular or plural before placing the apostrophe, and verify clause boundaries around every comma.

misconceptionFamilies.label: Doing the Work for Students Instead of Scaffolding Independent Thinking
misconceptionFamilies.description: Helping a struggling reader, writer, or math learner by supplying the final answer, rewriting the student's sentence, or completing calculation steps for them instead of giving a targeted hint, modeling one parallel step, or prompting self-correction.
misconceptionFamilies.remediationMove: Keep the cognitive pencil in the student's hand: offer the smallest effective prompt (chunking directions, pointing to a strategy anchor, asking a guiding question, or modeling one step) so the learner completes the target skill.

misconceptionFamilies.label: Crossing Teacher-Directed Paraprofessional Scope and Instructional Boundaries
misconceptionFamilies.description: Selecting classroom-application choices where a paraprofessional independently designs core curriculum, modifies IEP goals or grading policies, diagnoses a learning disability, or delivers unapproved parent evaluations instead of reinforcing teacher-planned instruction and reporting observations to the supervising teacher.
misconceptionFamilies.remediationMove: Apply the ParaPro role filter to every classroom scenario: paraprofessionals reinforce teacher-planned lessons, guide small-group practice, check student understanding, and share objective observations with the licensed teacher—never replace teacher authority on curriculum, diagnosis, IEP changes, or formal grading.

misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.familyLabel: Confusing Passage Main Idea with Supporting Details or Outside Assumptions
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.title: Ground Every ParaPro Reading Answer in Explicit Text and Table Evidence
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.recognitionCue: A short passage, school announcement, lab procedure, or checkout table is followed by an option that sounds true in real life ("students should always recycle") or quotes one detail while missing what the entire passage is mostly about.
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.repairQuestion: Which exact sentence, procedural step, or table entry proves this choice—and does it reflect the whole text rather than one minor detail or personal opinion?

stages.label: Recognize
stages.instruction: Classify every reading distractor as either an Outside Assumption (not stated in the text), a Single Narrow Detail, or a Fact/Opinion confusion before picking an answer.
stages.requiredOutput: Cite the exact line or table cell that verifies the right answer and identify the unstated assumption inside the main trap choice.

stages.label: Repair
stages.instruction: Contrast main idea (the unifying message covering beginning, middle, and end) with supporting detail (one step, example, or statistic), and distinguish verifiable fact from value-judgment opinion.
stages.requiredOutput: Write a 3-point verification checklist: (1) stated or directly implied in text, (2) matches the full passage scope, (3) uses neutral verifiable proof for fact items.

stages.label: Targeted practice
stages.instruction: Inspect a 4-day classroom book-checkout table (Mon. 18, Tue. 22, Wed. 15, Thu. 25) and a notice moving band rehearsal to the auditorium; separate one valid conclusion from one unsupported assumption for each text.
stages.requiredOutput: State one text-verified conclusion for each stimulus (for example, Thursday had the highest checkout total at 25 books) and explain why assuming "Wednesday had a snow day" is invalid.

stages.label: Retry & transfer
stages.instruction: Apply the evidence-pointing habit to a vocabulary-in-context sentence using a contrast signal ("Although Nia was eager to perform, she was reluctant to sing a solo") and a multi-step science procedure.
stages.requiredOutput: Use the contrast clue to define the target word accurately and verify step sequence without skipping or importing outside rules.

misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.familyLabel: Adding Fraction Denominators Directly and Misapplying Percent or Decimal Place Value
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.title: Master No-Calculator Fractions, Decimals, and Percent Bases for ParaPro
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.recognitionCue: A non-calculator ParaPro math item pairs unlike fractions (such as 3/4 + 1/8), decimal division (4.8 ÷ 0.6), place-value digits (42.681), or a percentage of a whole number (35% of 80), and lists 4/12 or 0.8 as classic trap options.
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.repairQuestion: Are the fraction pieces the same size (common denominator), have both decimal numbers been scaled by the same power of 10, and what is the 100% whole for the percent?

stages.label: Recognize
stages.instruction: Spot the three highest-frequency no-calculator slips: adding denominators straight across, misplacing the decimal point after dividing by a number less than 1, and confusing tenths with hundredths.
stages.requiredOutput: Explain why 3/4 + 1/8 cannot equal 4/12 (4/12 is less than 3/4!) using a quick benchmark reasonableness estimate.

stages.label: Repair
stages.instruction: Review the exact no-calculator mechanics: rewrite 3/4 as 6/8 before adding 1/8 = 7/8; multiply both 4.8 and 0.6 by 10 to compute 48 ÷ 6 = 8; decompose percents into friendly benchmarks (35% of 80 = 10% × 3 + 5% = 24 + 4 = 28).
stages.requiredOutput: Write one benchmark-estimation check for each operation so an off-by-10 decimal error or shrunken fraction sum is caught immediately.

stages.label: Targeted practice
stages.instruction: Compute without a calculator: (1) 3/4 + 1/8, (2) 4.8 ÷ 0.6, (3) the place value of 8 in 42.681, and (4) 35% of 80, plus the number halfway between 0.4 and 0.5.
stages.requiredOutput: Show the clean mental/paper setup yielding 7/8, 8, hundredths (0.08), 28, and 0.45.

stages.label: Retry & transfer
stages.instruction: Compare two rational numbers in mixed forms (such as 3/4 vs. 0.72 or 5/8 vs. 0.65) and convert a decimal to a reduced fraction without a calculator.
stages.requiredOutput: Convert both values to a common representation (both decimals or common-denominator fractions) and prove which comparison statement is true.

misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.familyLabel: Breaking Equation Balance, Order of Operations, and Area vs. Perimeter Distinctions
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.title: Enforce Order of Operations, Balanced Equations, and Perimeter vs. Area
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.recognitionCue: A ParaPro math item combines subtraction and multiplication (18 − 3 × 4), presents an exponent (2⁵), asks to solve a two-step equation, or describes fencing vs. carpeting a rectangular garden.
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.repairQuestion: Did multiplication and exponents run before subtraction, did both sides of the equation receive the exact same inverse operation, and does the prompt ask for outer boundary length (perimeter) or interior square coverage (area)?

stages.label: Recognize
stages.instruction: Identify left-to-right arithmetic traps (18 − 3 first), base-times-exponent errors (2⁵ → 10), one-sided equation steps, and perimeter/area formula swaps before computing.
stages.requiredOutput: Label the trap baked into the distractor (for example, 60 comes from subtracting before multiplying; 10 comes from multiplying base by exponent).

stages.label: Repair
stages.instruction: Anchor four concrete rules: exponents mean repeated multiplication of the base (2⁵ = 2×2×2×2×2 = 32); multiplication precedes addition/subtraction; an equation is a balance scale requiring identical inverse operations on both sides; perimeter adds all boundary edges (units) while area multiplies perpendicular dimensions (square units).
stages.requiredOutput: Write a side-by-side comparison of perimeter (2l + 2w, fencing/trim) vs. area (l × w, tile/carpet) for a 6 ft by 4 ft rectangle.

stages.label: Targeted practice
stages.instruction: Solve four no-calculator checks: (1) 18 − 3 × 4, (2) 2⁵, (3) 684 − 297 with regrouping verification, and (4) solve 3x + 5 = 20 while verifying by substitution.
stages.requiredOutput: Record the step-by-step results (6, 32, 387 verified by 387 + 297 = 684, and x = 5 verified by 3(5) + 5 = 20).

stages.label: Retry & transfer
stages.instruction: Solve a classroom word problem requiring both choosing the right measurement (border ribbon vs. poster surface) and setting up a balanced equation for a missing side length.
stages.requiredOutput: State whether perimeter or area applies, show the balanced inverse step, and include the correct linear or square unit.

misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.familyLabel: Missing Comma Splices, Homophone Mix-Ups, and Subject-Verb Agreement Errors
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.title: Eliminate Homophone, Apostrophe, Agreement, and Clause-Join Errors
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.recognitionCue: A ParaPro Writing question tests "they're/their/there," "then/than," plural possessives ("teachers'"), dangling modifiers, or comma splices where a wrong option sounds completely normal when read aloud.
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.repairQuestion: When you expand contractions, isolate the core subject, check singular vs. plural ownership, and test whether each side of a comma is a full sentence, which option stays 100% standard?

stages.label: Recognize
stages.instruction: Read Writing items visually rather than by ear alone: underline every homophone pair, apostrophe, verb-subject pair, and clause boundary.
stages.requiredOutput: Pinpoint the exact mechanical category tested (homophone, possessive apostrophe, agreement, dangling modifier, tense shift, or comma splice).

stages.label: Repair
stages.instruction: Apply rapid mechanical tests: "they're" = "they are," "their" = ownership, "there" = place; "than" = comparison, "then" = time sequence; plural nouns ending in -s take the apostrophe after the s ("two teachers' plans"); two independent clauses need a period, semicolon, or comma + FANBOYS.
stages.requiredOutput: Write one contrast pair for each rule (such as "faster than" vs. "finish math, then read" and "the teacher's desk" vs. "two teachers' lesson plans").

stages.label: Targeted practice
stages.instruction: Edit three ParaPro-style sentences: (1) fix "there/their/they're" in a sentence about students putting coats in lockers, (2) repair a dangling hallway modifier ("Walking through the hallway, the bulletin board caught Maya's eye"), and (3) fix a comma splice joining two closely related independent clauses.
stages.requiredOutput: Provide all three corrected sentences and name the mechanical check that verifies each edit.

stages.label: Retry & transfer
stages.instruction: Complete a mixed proofreading item combining direct-quotation punctuation, pronoun clarity, and parts-of-speech identification ("carefully" modifying a verb vs. adjective modifying a noun).
stages.requiredOutput: Select the error-free sentence, place quotation marks and commas accurately, and classify the target word by its syntactic job in the sentence.

misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.familyLabel: Doing the Work for Students Instead of Scaffolding Independent Thinking
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.title: Coach Student Independence with Graduated Scaffolds Instead of Rescuing
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.recognitionCue: A ParaPro classroom-application vignette shows a student stuck on a word problem, decoding word, or draft paragraph, and the tempting "helpful" distractor has the paraprofessional give the answer, rewrite the sentence, or excuse the student from trying.
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.repairQuestion: Does this paraprofessional move build the student's own strategy so they can take the next step themselves, or does it take the learning task out of the student's hands?

stages.label: Recognize
stages.instruction: Spot "rescue" distractors in classroom-support stems: telling the student the answer, writing on the student's paper, simplifying away the target skill, or abandoning the student with zero guidance ("try harder").
stages.requiredOutput: Label each option as Rescue (over-helping), Neglect (no support), or Effective Scaffold (guided student ownership).

stages.label: Repair
stages.instruction: Structure a 3-step paraprofessional scaffolding ladder: (1) ask the student to show or explain where they got stuck, (2) offer a concrete tool or prompt (reread step 2, underline clue words, use a place-value chart or sound-out cue), (3) let the student execute and verify the step independently.
stages.requiredOutput: Write one effective scaffolding question for reading comprehension, one for fraction/order-of-operations math, and one for student writing revision.

stages.label: Targeted practice
stages.instruction: Respond to two realistic vignettes: (1) a fifth grader writes 3/4 + 1/8 = 4/12 during teacher-assigned small-group practice; (2) a fourth grader's draft has a comma splice and missing topic detail.
stages.requiredOutput: Script a two-sentence paraprofessional prompt for each student that guides them to discover the error using visual models or read-aloud checks without telling them the final fix.

stages.label: Retry & transfer
stages.instruction: Evaluate a new classroom-support item where a student misreads multi-step lab instructions or gets overwhelmed by a graphic organizer.
stages.requiredOutput: Choose the scaffold that breaks the task into manageable steps while keeping the student responsible for reading, calculating, or revising.

misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.familyLabel: Crossing Teacher-Directed Paraprofessional Scope and Instructional Boundaries
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.title: Stay Inside Teacher-Directed Paraprofessional Scope and Reporting Roles
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.recognitionCue: A ParaPro scenario involves a struggling learner, a parent asking for an evaluation, or a student needing a different assignment—and a proactive-sounding distractor has the paraprofessional rewrite the lesson plan, change IEP accommodations, assign report-card grades, or diagnose a disability.
misconceptionRemediationPlaybooks.repairQuestion: Is this action within a paraprofessional's supervised instructional-support role, or does it cross into the licensed teacher's or IEP team's legal authority?

stages.label: Recognize
stages.instruction: Scan classroom-application choices for scope-violation verbs: "diagnose," "modify the IEP," "design a new curriculum unit," "assign final grades," or "tell the parent the student has dyslexia."
stages.requiredOutput: Flag every authority boundary crossed by the distractor and name who holds legal responsibility for that decision.

stages.label: Repair
stages.instruction: Divide classroom duties cleanly into Paraprofessional Scope (implementing teacher-designed plans, facilitating small-group practice, modeling approved strategies, collecting objective anecdotal/accuracy data, alerting the teacher) vs. Licensed Teacher/Team Scope (initial instruction of new standards, grading, formal assessment interpretation, IEP changes, parent conferences on eligibility).
stages.requiredOutput: Write a 2-column role boundary card plus one polite script for redirecting a parent's diagnostic or grading question to the supervising teacher.

stages.label: Targeted practice
stages.instruction: Decide the compliant paraprofessional response in three vignettes: (1) a student finishes teacher-assigned practice with 40% accuracy on fraction addition, (2) a parent asks at pickup whether their child needs special education testing, (3) a student's IEP accommodation seems unclear during a quiz.
stages.requiredOutput: Specify the exact in-scope action for all three cases: document specific error patterns and notify the teacher, refer the parent warmly to the teacher/team without speculating, and verify the accommodation directly with the teacher before altering test conditions.

stages.label: Retry & transfer
stages.instruction: Evaluate a fresh ParaPro scenario balancing proactive student support against professional boundaries during small-group literacy or math work.
stages.requiredOutput: Select the option that pairs immediate teacher-aligned support with objective communication back to the supervising teacher, rejecting both passive inaction and overstepping.
